title: 2.6 Proving Geometric Relationships

icans: I can use the Right Angles Congruence Theorem.
I can use the Congruent Supplements and Congruent Complements Theorems.
I can prove and use the Vertical Angles Congruence Theorem.

vocab: a proof that uses boxes and arrows to show the flow of a logical ___________
a proof written as ____________ in a paragraph

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: supplements of the same angle

blocks.p: Draw two crossing lines. Number the angles 1, 2, 3, 4 going around. Measure ∠1, ∠2, and ∠3.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Right Angles Congruence Theorem: all right angles are _______________.

blocks.stem: ∠ABC and ∠DEF are right angles. What can you conclude, and why?

notes: Congruent Supplements Theorem: if two angles are supplementary to the same angle (or to congruent angles), then they are _______________. The Congruent Complements Theorem works the same way.

blocks.stem: ∠1 and ∠2 are supplementary, and ∠3 and ∠2 are supplementary. m∠1 = 47°. Find m∠3 and explain in a paragraph proof.

notes: Vertical Angles Congruence Theorem is proved with the _______________ Postulate and the Congruent Supplements Theorem.

blocks.stem: Given: ∠5 and ∠7 are vertical angles.  Prove: ∠5 ≅ ∠7.
Two lines intersect. Two vertical angles measure (5x + 10)° and (7x − 18)°. Find x and all four angle measures.
∠4 and ∠5 are complementary, and ∠6 and ∠5 are complementary. m∠4 = 28°. Find m∠6 and name the theorem.
Two vertical angles measure (3x + 20)° and (5x − 10)°. Find x, the angle measure, and the measure of an angle that forms a linear pair with it.

tickets.stem: ∠A and ∠C are both supplementary to ∠B. m∠A = 63°. Find m∠C.
Vertical angles measure (4x)° and (2x + 30)°. Find x and the angle measure.
